❓ FAQ

Repeated same-name elements?
Converted to an array to keep multiple values.
Is order preserved?
Usually yes — XML is ordered, and a YAML mapping keeps insertion order after parsing, so most tools output in document order. But note: once it passes through a "sort by keys" intermediate step (some libraries do this), order is lost; if the downstream depends on order (e.g., config item precedence), check and preserve the original order after conversion.

map.XML → JSON：先剔除注释、处理指令并把 CDATA 段还原为文本；对每个: XML → JSON: comments and processing instructions are removed and CDATA sections are restored to text; for each element the header between < and > is taken, a trailing / marks self-closing, the tag name is everything before the first whitespace, and the rest is extracted as attributes with ([\w:-]+)\s*=\s*\"([^\"]*)\"; child nodes are grouped by tag name, a single occurrence taking a single value and multiple taking an array; attributes go into the object with an @ prefix and text with the #text key; a missing root node or a parse failure shows an error. JSON → XML: object values restore @-prefixed keys as attributes and #text as text, arrays are serialized as same-named elements one by one; when there is more than one top-level key the result is wrapped in <root>. YAML scalar restoration rules: strip paired quotes, true/false become booleans, null and ~ become empty, pure integers use parseInt, pure decimals use parseFloat, and everything else stays a string; strings containing : # - [ ] { } , or leading/trailing whitespace, starting with a digit, or equal to true/false/null are double-quoted
